transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Recording: yes (auto)
Attendees: Marcus Liu (Redwood AE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Karen Blake (CISO, Oxford Savings), Tom Reeves (Head of Cloud Ops), Aisha Rahman (Legal)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Oxford Savings is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary concerns are EU/UK data residency for some retail products, strict logging retention limits for regulated financial data, and HIPAA-like controls for a small health-savings product. They asked about SOC 2, ISO, encryption/KMS, and options for Private (VPC) or on-prem. Next steps: share compliance pack, pricing for Dedicated, schedule technical deep dive and run benchmarks on sample traffic.

Topics:
- Data residency (EU/UK vs US)
- Logging/audit retention and masking
- Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM options
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private trade-offs (latency, cost, isolation)
- Compliance docs: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA flowdown

Action items (captured in call):
- Marcus to send SOC2/HIPAA pack & architecture notes (by 2026-03-05)
- Olivia to estimate latency/cost for sample workload on Dedicated (by 2026-03-11)
- Tom to share list of in-scope products & regional residency constraints (by 2026-03-08)

Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros — I'm Marcus, AE at Redwood, with Olivia our SE.
[00:18] Karen: Hi, Karen Blake, CISO at Oxford Savings. We run a handful of retail and commercial products, some of which have EU/UK residency requirements.
[00:25] Tom: Tom Reeves, I own cloud ops. We're interested in understanding the deploy models and what we can keep in-region.
[00:32] Aisha: Aisha here from Legal, I'll be checking the compliance flowdowns and any data processing agreements.
[00:37] Olivia: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to surface residency and logging constraints and then we'll map Redwood's Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options to your requirements.

[02:12] Marcus: Quick product overview: Redwood Hosted is our managed API, fastest to get started. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and capacity isolation. And Redwood Private is a customer-managed control plane for VPC or on-prem installs.
[02:43] Karen: Okay, so for our EU retail dataset we need all raw data to stay within the UK/EU. No cross-border logs unless they're anonymized.
[02:58] Marcus: Understood. We do have region pinning for deployments; with Dedicated or Private you can restrict compute to a specific cloud region or on-prem cluster. Hosted can be region-restricted for certain plans but persists in our control plane — is that a hard no?
[03:20] Karen: For certain products, we can't have any PII leave the EU. So Hosted where logs or retention lives in the US is difficult.
[03:28] Olivia: For that case, Dedicated in a UK/EU region or Private (VPC) is usually what we recommend; Dedicated gives you predictable performance without managing the infra. Private gives max control if you need customer-managed KMS/HSM.

[05:05] Tom: Can you elaborate on logging and audit log retention? We have internal rules to retain audit trails for 7 years but some logs can't contain certain raw fields.
[05:20] Marcus: Our platform keeps request/response logs for debugging/audit and you can configure retention. For Hosted we default to 90 days; for Dedicated you can configure retention windows and set scrubbing/masking.
[05:40] Aisha: Do you support selective logging/masking at ingest? For example, mask account numbers, truncate messages, or drop certain fields before they hit logs?
[05:53] Olivia: Yes, we offer request transformers and optional redaction—pre-processing hooks that can strip or hash fields before they're stored in logs. For Dedicated and Private you can also run those transformers in your VPC so logs never leave your environment.

[08:10] Karen: About encryption: we need customer-managed keys, HSM-backed where possible. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[08:22] Marcus: Absolutely. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM and control keys. For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS in many cloud providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we can document the envelope encryption flow. For Hosted we offer BYOK for certain enterprise tiers, but the key lifecycle is still managed by the cloud provider and some customers prefer Private for full control.

[10:44] Tom: Latency/cost tradeoff — we have some low-latency chat features where 95th p99 latency matters. How does Dedicated compare to Hosted?
[10:56] Olivia: Dedicated typically gives you lower and more consistent latency because you control a reserved GPU pool and there's less noisy neighbor effect. Hosted is optimized but multitenant, so latency is good but not as tightly bounded; we provide SLOs on enterprise tiers. Also Dedicated can be tuned with batching and quantization profiles.
[11:20] Tom: And Private? On-prem will be best for latency but adds ops overhead.
[11:25] Olivia: Correct. Private means you're running the runtime in your network — best latency and control but you operate it.

[13:05] Karen: GDPR specific question: if a user requests deletion, what is the flow to ensure we can purge data from logs and model caches (KV cache)?
[13:20] Marcus: We have deletion APIs that delete request logs and can invalidate KV caches. For Hosted we run the delete in our control plane and provide attestations. For Dedicated and Private you have direct control to purge caches and logs. Note: inference outputs may be part of downstream systems so we'd coordinate on retention across the whole stack.
[13:45] Aisha: Do you provide Data Processing Agreements and standard SCCs?
[13:50] Marcus: Yes, we provide DPAs and SCC templates and can add flow-down language for Dedicated/Private customers; we'll include those in the compliance pack.

[16:01] Tom: Operationally, if we pick Dedicated in eu-west-2, how are upgrades handled? We need maintenance windows and a canary rollout for model changes.
[16:14] Olivia: Dedicated supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallbacks. You define the policy; we can do in-region upgrades during windows you choose. For Private you control upgrades entirely.

[18:30] Karen: Anything around HIPAA? We have a small HSA product and need Business Associate Agreement considerations. Can Redwood sign BAAs?
[18:45] Marcus: Yes, we have customers on HIPAA workloads. We can sign BAAs and our compliance pack includes the HIPAA safeguards. For the HSA product you might want Dedicated or Private depending on how much control you want over PHI handling—Hosted can work if we sign a BAA and you pick the enterprise plan with strict retention and BYOK.

[21:12] Tom: There's also a question on telemetry: does Redwood send telemetry back to Redwood for runtime improvements and if so, can we opt out?
[21:25] Olivia: We collect anonymized telemetry for quality; Dedicated and Private give you full control to disable telemetry. For Hosted, telemetry is on by default but can be restricted on enterprise contracts.

[23:00] Aisha: From Legal, we need to see sample SLAs, data processing, subprocessor list, and simple language on liability and data deletion proofs.
[23:15] Marcus: We'll include those in the pack. Also include SOC 2 Type II report and ISO certs where applicable.

[25:40] Karen: On retention limits — for some regulated logs, we cannot store full messages in cleartext in logs, only hashed pointers. Is that supported?
[25:55] Olivia: Yes, request transformations can hash or tokenize fields, and you can configure redaction rules. For Dedicated/Private you can push those transformers into the VPC so logs never contain the raw text.

[28:00] Tom: Can we route requests based on policy — e.g., low-risk queries to Hosted for cost savings, and high-risk EU queries to Dedicated in-region?
[28:12] Marcus: Yes, smart routing is core to the platform. You can set routing policies by region, latency, cost, or customer tier. We also support automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained.

[30:45] Karen: About audit logs and compliance reviews — do you provide immutable audit trails and exportable logs for auditors?
[30:58] Olivia: We provide audit logs that are tamper-evident and exportable. For Dedicated/Private you can ship logs to your own SIEM and control retention. We also have integrations with common log stores.

[33:10] Aisha: If we run a pilot, what minimal data can we use for benchmarking to avoid sending PII?
[33:25] Olivia: Best practice is to synthetic-ize or token‑mask PII in sample sets. We can run performance benchmarks with masked data and provide latency/cost metrics. We'll also give guidance on sample sizes to simulate production load.

[35:40] Marcus: Quick pricing note — Dedicated is priced on reserved GPU capacity with commit tiers; Hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll send a sample pricing grid and committed discount tiers.

[37:18] Tom: On identity — SSO and RBAC integration?
[37:25] Marcus: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access. For Private you can plug into your identity provider directly.

[39:05] Karen: OK, this is helpful. My priorities: get SOC2/HIPAA docs, confirm residency architecture for EU retail products, and ensure log redaction options.
[39:18] Marcus: Great — we'll send the compliance pack and a proposed Dedicated configuration in eu-west-2, plus a timeline for a technical deep dive.

[40:00] Olivia: I'll also estimate latency and cost for your sample workload and share a suggested batching/quantization profile to meet your p95/p99 numbers.

[41:05] Karen: Sounds good. Aisha and Tom will coordinate the data residency requirements and sample datasets.

[41:30] Marcus: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

End of recording.
